questions.q: Name the salt: iron + hydrochloric acid.
questions.model: The metal gives the first name: iron. Hydrochloric acid gives 'chloride'. So iron chloride.

questions.q: What is the test for hydrogen?
questions.a: A lit splint gives a squeaky pop

questions.q: Why does copper not fizz in dilute acid?
Write word equations for six metal and acid pairs on the sheet. Mark any that do not react.
questions.a: Correct salts and hydrogen; copper/gold pairs marked 'no reaction'
questions.model: Teacher writes the first: 'zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + hydrogen'.

questions.q: Use the demonstration observations to order magnesium, zinc, iron and copper by reactivity with acid.
Why are acid reactions used to test how reactive a metal is, rather than water reactions?
questions.a: Many metals barely react with water but do with acid, so differences are easier to see

questions.q: Metal + acid makes a salt and...
Big question: why not store vinegar in a metal tin?
questions.a: Vinegar is an acid and can react with the metal.
